title: ASS-to-SRT dependency atlas assets omit current core/subtitles consumers
observed_behavior: A fresh non-mutating render from current Python imports produces a structurally different pipeline/ass_to_srt diagram with current incoming core/subtitles edges. The checked-in SVG has no core/subtitles node and 11 edge groups; the fresh generator reports 14 shown edges and adds external_core_subtitles connections. Both fresh PNG and SVG hashes differ from the assigned assets.
expected_invariant: Generated dependency navigation must represent the current import graph, or carry an explicit stale finding, so agents do not mistake an obsolete diagram for current module ownership and consumers.
root_cause: The dependency atlas was not regenerated after the scratch subtitle-stage module began importing ASS-to-SRT package helpers.
failure_scenario: An agent uses the focused atlas to assess ASS helper callers and concludes the package is isolated from core/subtitles. It misses the active scratch-stage consumer and makes an incomplete compatibility, placement, or test-impact decision.
evidence: A temporary Graphviz reproduction used collect_data(DEFAULT_PACKAGE_ROOTS), render_detail_dot, and run_dot without writing the repository.
The fresh render reported pipeline/ass_to_srt nodes=6 and edges=14 with no AST parse errors.
The current SVG contains 11 edge groups and no external_core_subtitles or core/subtitles label.
Fresh/current hashes differ for both PNG (4c413d... versus 949409...) and SVG (03c6e9... versus d4f6d7...).
The adjacent pipeline/ass_to_srt_cli PNG reproduced exactly; its SVG was text-identical after newline normalization, isolating substantive drift to this package diagram.
existing_safeguards: Generated summaries for individual ASS helper files list current imports.
Source and caller tests remain authoritative.
The atlas is documented as a query aid rather than executable truth.
safeguard_gap: The image itself has no freshness marker or stale warning, and its missing incoming edge is precisely the relationship an atlas consumer seeks.
tests_present: tests/python/tooling/test_dependency_atlas.py covers generator structure and output helpers.
tests_missing: Non-mutating generator --check mode for tracked atlas assets
CI exact or semantic graph reconciliation for focused diagrams
Freshness assertion for the core/subtitles to pipeline/ass_to_srt dependency
recommended_remediation: Regenerate the dependency atlas through the canonical tool and add a non-mutating --check mode that compares graph semantics before image serialization. Treat newline-only SVG differences as normalized-equivalent but fail when nodes or edges differ.
remediation_risk: Low: the change is generated documentation only, but a full atlas regeneration may touch many assets because Graphviz layout or line endings vary. Review semantic graph diffs separately from serialization noise.
validation_rung: Run dependency-atlas tooling tests, regenerate in a disposable tree or --check mode, compare node/edge semantics and then exact tracked outputs, and validate generated-document links. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit generated-artifact finding; neither archived W05 report assessed dependency-atlas freshness.

title: ASS-to-SRT CLI accepts its source as an output and atomically replaces it
observed_behavior: The CLI resolves arbitrary input, SRT-output, and summary-output paths but never proves that they are disjoint or that a destination is absent. Both SRT and summary writes end in os.replace, which overwrites an existing destination. A synthetic current-code probe passed one temporary source.mkv path as both input and output; parse_args accepted it and atomic_write_text replaced the original bytes.
expected_invariant: A subtitle helper must never overwrite source media or an unrelated pre-existing file by default. Source and diagnostic/output paths must be canonically disjoint, and replacement of an existing destination must require a separately named, validated policy.
root_cause: Destination commit is implemented as unconditional replacement while CLI path parsing validates only presence, not canonical identity, source-boundary separation, or no-clobber intent.
failure_scenario: An operator or caller accidentally supplies the source MKV as the positional SRT output or --summary-json path. Extraction can complete and the final atomic replace destroys the source media with subtitle text or diagnostic JSON, without a safe-delete policy or mutation confirmation.
evidence: Lines 187-200 create a sibling temporary file and call os.replace(tmp_name, target) unconditionally.
Lines 571-577 accept input and output strings without same-file, existing-target, or source-root checks.
Lines 832-836 commit the SRT and optional summary through the same overwriting helper.
A bundled-Python synthetic probe reported input_equals_output=true and showed the original temporary source bytes replaced by rendered SRT text.
affected_flows: PowerShell or Python callers that forward operator-selected paths
existing_safeguards: The production PowerShell caller normally chooses a generated scratch destination.
The write is atomic, so partial destination contents are unlikely.
Temporary files are removed on write failure.
safeguard_gap: Atomicity protects write completeness but not target identity. A conventional caller path does not protect direct CLI use or future callers, and no backend/source-boundary guard is enforced inside the mutation-capable helper.
tests_present: tests/python/core/subtitles/test_ass_to_srt_helpers.py covers conversion helpers and output rendering.
tests_missing: CLI rejection when input and SRT output resolve to the same file
CLI rejection when --summary-json aliases the input or SRT output
default no-clobber behavior for an existing destination
Windows case-insensitive and symlink/junction alias coverage
recommended_remediation: Resolve all three paths using the repository path-identity rules, reject any input/output/summary alias, and use a no-replace commit by default. If overwrite is ever required, expose it as a strict explicit option that still cannot target the source or a protected source root.
remediation_risk: Medium: changing existing-destination behavior may affect rerun workflows that currently rely on replacement. Preserve those workflows through an explicit scratch-only overwrite mode with collision and identity tests.
validation_rung: Focused bundled-Python CLI/path-identity tests using temporary text fixtures, existing-destination and alias races, followed by the ASS helper suite and subtitle conversion smokes. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root; the archived W05 media-policy reviews did not identify CLI source/output aliasing.

title: Completed subtitle QA treats boolean output_exists=false as a passing result
observed_behavior: _text converts value or an empty string, so boolean False becomes an empty string. The later comparison to the literal string false therefore never fires for the boolean emitted by completed-row services. A synthetic completed row with output_exists=False and otherwise valid one-cue conversion evidence returned posture pass.
expected_invariant: An explicit boolean false output-existence proof must block completed subtitle QA because conversion evidence cannot be trusted when the completed output is missing.
root_cause: A generic text-normalization helper uses truthiness instead of preserving typed false values, while the caller tests only the normalized string false.
failure_scenario: A completed output is deleted or becomes unavailable after its decision evidence was recorded. The backend supplies output_exists=false, but subtitle QA reports pass and tells the operator only that completed decision evidence is present.
evidence: Lines 69-70 implement str(value or empty-string), collapsing False and zero.
Lines 586-588 block only when _casefold(output_exists) equals the string false.
Completed-manifest tests elsewhere assert that output_exists is a real boolean and can be False.
A bundled-Python probe with boolean False returned posture=pass and reason Completed subtitle decision evidence is present.
existing_safeguards: Other completed-row fields can add blocking failures.
String value false would take the intended branch.
Completed services separately expose output existence.
safeguard_gap: The exact typed value used by the completed service bypasses the only missing-output QA block, and existing QA tests cover only output_exists=True.
tests_present: tests/python/desktop/test_subtitle_qa_feature.py covers successful, OCR-failed, and verifier-mismatch completed QA with output_exists=True.
Completed service tests verify that false booleans can be emitted.
tests_missing: Completed subtitle QA with output_exists=False as a boolean
Typed normalization tests for False, zero, None, and the string false
End-to-end completed-row QA refresh after output deletion
recommended_remediation: Test row.get('output_exists') is False before text normalization, or change _text to preserve false as 'False' and add explicit typed handling. Keep None distinct as unknown rather than missing.
remediation_risk: Low: the intended string-false branch already establishes the desired posture. The main compatibility risk is distinguishing absent/None evidence from explicit false.
validation_rung: Focused subtitle QA unit tests for boolean false, string false, None, and valid true evidence, followed by the completed-row QA service/API tests. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root; no current or archived W05 finding covered typed completed-QA existence evidence.

title: Python planning returns a runnable remux decision when audio is missing and AllowNoAudio is false
observed_behavior: The planner hard-blocks a missing video stream but creates audio actions solely by iterating source.audio_streams. When the list is empty it emits no audio action, no hard rule, and no rejection even if effective_policy.allow_no_audio is false. A synthetic no-audio fixture returned REMUX with an empty audio action list.
expected_invariant: When policy forbids no-audio output, every authoritative decision and dry-run plan must reject a source with no audio before presenting a runnable copy, remux, or encode route.
root_cause: The Python routing reducer has no source-audio cardinality rule and never consumes EffectiveDecisionPolicy.allow_no_audio during decision construction.
failure_scenario: The UI or orchestration planner previews a normal remux for a silent or incompletely probed source under the default false policy. Execution later reaches the PowerShell audio guard and fails, so the backend-authored plan and runtime policy contradict each other.
evidence: Lines 55-63 contain an explicit missing-video rejection, but lines 68-70 only map whatever audio streams exist.
AllowNoAudio is accepted by decision_policy_from_mapping, yet the routing module has no allow_no_audio branch.
A bundled-Python probe removed all audio streams from a current fixture and returned route REMUX, legacy remux, zero audio actions, and no audio-missing reason.
src/mediapipeline/core/orchestration/planner.py consumes this decision to build dry-run steps.
existing_safeguards: The PowerShell Build-AudioArgs runtime blocks missing audio when AllowNoAudio is false.
A missing video stream is rejected by the Python planner.
Presence-probe failures fail closed at runtime.
safeguard_gap: A later runtime rejection does not repair a misleading backend plan, and the Python plan contains neither the expected block nor an explicit audio-omission action.
tests_present: tests/python/core/decide/test_processing_decision.py covers video absence and several populated-audio policies.
tests/python/integration/test_ffmpeg_media_policy_regression_matrix.py compares populated audio actions.
ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-AudioPolicyChecks.ps1 covers the PowerShell runtime guard.
tests_missing: Python decision with zero audio streams and allow_no_audio=False
Python decision with zero audio streams and allow_no_audio=True plus explicit omit evidence
Plan/runtime parity case for silent sources
recommended_remediation: Add a source-audio cardinality rule before action construction. Reject with a stable hard-block reason when audio is absent and policy is false; when true, emit an explicit omit-all/not-applicable action or equivalent structured evidence that downstream planners preserve.
remediation_risk: Medium: a new reject route affects previews and any callers that treated an empty audio list as implicit omission. Align reason codes and schemas with the existing PowerShell policy before rollout.
validation_rung: Focused processing-decision and orchestration-plan tests for zero-audio sources under both policy values, regression-matrix coverage, and the synthetic PowerShell audio-policy checks. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root; archived W05 reviews did not cover Python no-audio plan/runtime parity.

title: Python routing ignores subtitle_mode=convert_preferred and plans copies instead of conversion
observed_behavior: subtitle_action implements drop, forced burn, MP4 compatibility, and otherwise copy. It never branches on convert_preferred. A current image-subtitle fixture planned under subtitle_mode=convert_preferred returned REMUX with both subtitle actions set to copy and no converted streams.
expected_invariant: A configured preferred-subtitle conversion mode must be represented explicitly in backend-authored stream actions and planned output; it must not be silently treated as keep/copy.
root_cause: The subtitle decision reducer treats every non-drop, non-burn MKV policy as the same default copy mode and has no implementation for the declared convert_preferred mode.
failure_scenario: An operator selects preferred-language SRT generation. The Python preview reports only copied embedded subtitles and no conversion work, while the PowerShell runtime follows richer conversion policy or the requested sidecar is never represented in the plan.
evidence: processing_decision.py declares convert_preferred as a valid SubtitleMode.
Lines 76-160 check drop and burn behavior but fall through to a copy decision for MKV.
A bundled-Python probe with the current image-subtitle fixture returned subtitle_actions copy/copy and converted_streams empty.
Preset policy contract tests show convert_preferred and generatePreferredSrt are accepted configuration values.
existing_safeguards: The PowerShell subtitle engine has conversion and review paths.
MP4 image subtitles are separately rejected for explicit review.
Original subtitles remain copied by the default MKV path.
safeguard_gap: Preserving originals does not satisfy the additional configured SRT generation request, and the planner gives no warning that the mode is unsupported or deferred.
tests_present: tests/python/core/decide/test_processing_decision.py covers drop-like MP4 behavior and forced burn-in.
tests/python/core/contract/test_preset_policy_contract.py accepts convert_preferred configuration.
tests_missing: MKV convert_preferred action plan for preferred text subtitles
Image-subtitle OCR/review plan under convert_preferred
Language-selection and generatePreferredSrt parity between preset migration, Python decisions, and PowerShell execution
recommended_remediation: Model preferred-language selection and generated-sidecar work explicitly in EffectiveDecisionPolicy and SubtitleStreamDecision. Either emit conversion/OCR actions with review requirements or reject/defer with a stable unsupported-policy reason; never silently fall through to copy.
remediation_risk: High: subtitle selection, OCR, sidecars, and original preservation are release-sensitive. Reuse the existing PowerShell policy semantics and validate mixed text/image/language fixtures before changing execution.
validation_rung: Focused Python decision-contract and preset-parity tests, FFmpeg media-policy regression matrix, PowerShell subtitle builder/OCR tests, and synthetic sidecar evidence checks. Representative real-media validation is required before a production behavior change, but not to confirm this planning defect.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root; the archived W05 MP4 subtitle-kind finding concerned container conversion details, not the ignored Python convert_preferred mode.

title: Adjacent-cue merging silently deletes numeric-only SRT cue text
observed_behavior: The line parser treats every all-digit line as a cue index even while it is inside an active cue. Numeric subtitle text is therefore discarded and resets the current cue. If any later adjacent identical cues are merged, the function rewrites the file from its malformed in-memory cue list and permanently omits the numeric cue.
expected_invariant: Valid SRT cue text, including numeric-only dialogue such as years, room numbers, and counts, must survive cleanup and cue merging byte-semantically except for the explicitly merged duplicate timing interval.
root_cause: The ad hoc parser identifies cue indexes by lexical shape alone instead of by parser state and SRT block position.
failure_scenario: An OCR or converted SRT contains a cue whose complete text is 2026 and also contains any pair of adjacent identical cues elsewhere. Merge-AdjacentIdenticalCues collapses the pair, triggers a rewrite, and publishes an SRT in which the 2026 cue is gone.
evidence: Lines 266-277 interpret any trimmed digits-only line as a new cue index and clear current text/start state.
Lines 317-332 rewrite the full SRT whenever at least one adjacent pair merges.
A synthetic temporary SRT with a 2026 cue followed by two mergeable repeat cues was processed by the current function; output contained only one merged repeat cue and no 2026 text.
The probe used an OS-temporary text fixture and deleted it; no real media or repository state was mutated.
existing_safeguards: The function returns without rewriting when no cue pair is merged.
The rewritten file uses an atomic temporary commit.
Test-SrtFileUsable validates structural timing and nonempty text.
safeguard_gap: Structural validation cannot detect semantically missing dialogue, and one unrelated merge anywhere turns the parser mistake into a full-file destructive rewrite.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-VobSubSubtitleChecks.ps1 exercises adjacent identical text merging and validates ordinary SRT output.
tests_missing: Numeric-only cue text before, between, and after mergeable cues
Digits inside multiline cue text
Round-trip cue-count and text preservation assertions for the merger
recommended_remediation: Replace the lexical loop with a stateful SRT block parser that recognizes an optional numeric index only at block start immediately before a valid timing line. Preserve unknown text blocks fail-closed, and compare cue/text inventories before committing a rewrite.
remediation_risk: Medium: stricter parsing may reject malformed SRT that the current heuristic tolerates. Keep cleanup optional/fail-safe and retain the original file whenever parsing is ambiguous.
validation_rung: Focused PowerShell synthetic SRT tests for numeric, multiline, malformed, and mergeable cases plus VobSub/BDPGS subtitle unit checks. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root; archived W05 subtitle findings did not cover numeric cue-text loss in the merger.

title: Allowed no-audio returns leave prior-file audio globals active for remux consumers

locations.symbol: Build-AudioArgs dropped-audio return and state commit

observed_behavior: LastAudioDefaultIndex, LastAudioTrackCount, and LastAudioTranscodeActive are assigned only on the normal populated-audio path. Both allowed no-audio returns exit first, so a long-lived pipeline process retains values from the previous file. Downstream remux code reads those script globals as if they describe the current file.
expected_invariant: Every Build-AudioArgs outcome must publish a complete per-file audio state. A no-audio result must reset track count, default index, and transcode activity before downstream stages inspect them.
root_cause: Per-file audio decisions are stored in mutable script globals, and early successful omission branches return without initializing or clearing the consumer-visible global state.
failure_scenario: A file with transcoded audio is followed in the same process by a silent file allowed under AllowNoAudio. mkvmerge validation expects stale audio tracks and can refuse the no-audio mux; the FFmpeg AV stage can also acquire CPU controls because stale transcode activity remains true.
evidence: Lines 443-447 and 565-568 return -an before the assignments at lines 584-590.
remux_mkvmerge_args.ps1 lines 28-40 rejects when probed current audio TIDs are fewer than stale LastAudioTrackCount.
remux_ffmpeg_av_stage.ps1 lines 115 and 125 uses stale LastAudioTranscodeActive for CPU mutex/priority policy.
After the existing synthetic audio unit test established populated state, a current-code missing-audio/AllowNoAudio probe returned -an while Default=0, Count=1, and Transcode=true remained unchanged.
existing_safeguards: Missing audio is blocked unless AllowNoAudio is enabled.
The normal populated-audio branch writes all three globals.
Decision records expose an omit_all action for one early branch.
safeguard_gap: The explicit omit decision is separate from the legacy globals actually consumed by remux stages, and current tests assert -an but not state reset.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-AudioPolicyChecks.ps1 covers populated state and later allowed no-audio in one script.
ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-RemuxSplitStageChecks.ps1 covers remux stage construction.
tests_missing: Sequential populated-audio then allowed-no-audio assertion that all globals reset
All-streams-dropped AllowNoAudio reset
Remux consumer test proving zero expected audio tracks and no CPU transcode flag
recommended_remediation: Initialize one immutable per-file audio result at Build-AudioArgs entry and return it to consumers instead of relying on script globals. As an immediate fix, reset default index, track count, and transcode-active state before both successful no-audio returns and before any throwable probe path.
remediation_risk: Medium: legacy remux callers may depend on script-scope variables. Update all consumers atomically and validate sequential mixed-file processing.
validation_rung: Audio policy unit tests with sequential state assertions, remux mkvmerge/FFmpeg stage tests, process lifecycle smokes, and a synthetic multi-file sequence. Real media is not required for the reset; representative media is required before changing audio execution policy.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root; archived W05 audio review did not identify cross-file script-global leakage.

title: Missing mkvextract after MP4 VobSub staging leaks the staged temporary Matroska file
observed_behavior: For MP4-family input, Get-VobSubExtractionPair successfully stages the subtitle stream into temporary Matroska and records that path. If Resolve-VobSubMkvextractPath then fails, the returned failure object replaces TempFiles with an empty array. The caller finally block cleans only paths present in extract.TempFiles, so the staged file is orphaned.
expected_invariant: Every temporary artifact created before a subtitle prerequisite failure must remain attached to the returned cleanup manifest and be removed by the owning finally block.
root_cause: One early failure return reconstructs the extraction result with TempFiles empty instead of propagating the already accumulated extractTempFiles collection.
failure_scenario: FFmpeg staging is available but MKVToolNix/mkvextract is missing or becomes unavailable. Each attempted MP4 VobSub conversion leaves a staged .mkv in the processing directory, and repeated retries consume scratch disk until unrelated jobs fail.
evidence: Lines 698-702 populate extractTempFiles after successful MP4 staging.
Lines 708-710 return TempFiles=@() on missing mkvextract.
Lines 994-1000 clean only the TempFiles returned by the extraction result.
The VobSub unit test covers successful MP4 staging cleanup and later mkvextract execution failure, but no case where staging succeeds before resolver failure.
existing_safeguards: The caller has a finally cleanup loop.
Most later extraction failures propagate extractTempFiles.
Successful MP4 staging conversion is covered by a cleanup assertion.
safeguard_gap: The cleanup owner cannot infer an unreported path, and the exact missing-tool branch drops the only manifest reference before returning.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-VobSubSubtitleChecks.ps1 verifies successful MP4 staged-MKV cleanup and mkvextract command-failure evidence.
tests_missing: MP4 staging success followed by Resolve-VobSubMkvextractPath failure
Repeated failure proving no staged files accumulate
Cleanup propagation for every early extraction return
recommended_remediation: Return TempFiles=@($extractTempFiles) on the missing-tool branch and consolidate extraction failures through one result constructor that always carries accumulated temporaries. Add a finally-owned temp registry so later branches cannot omit created files.
remediation_risk: Low: the fix only expands cleanup metadata for a path already documented as temporary. Verify no returned path can reference source media.
validation_rung: Focused VobSub PowerShell unit tests with fake FFmpeg staging and missing mkvextract, exact temporary-directory inventory before/after, followed by subtitle OCR path-resolution checks. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root; archived W05 VobSub review did not cover staged-file loss on prerequisite resolution.

title: Optional seconv cleanup can block VobSub conversion forever because it has no timeout or stop path
observed_behavior: After OCR and cue merging, the optional seconv cleanup launches with Start-Process -Wait. Unlike the surrounding long-running subtitle commands, this branch has no timeout, stop-flag polling, heartbeat, guarded process-tree termination, or bounded wait.
expected_invariant: Every external subtitle tool invocation must have bounded execution, cooperative stop handling, progress/heartbeat evidence, and process-tree cleanup so close-readiness cannot wait indefinitely.
root_cause: An optional post-processing subprocess bypasses the repository native-command lifecycle wrapper and uses an unbounded synchronous Start-Process -Wait call.
failure_scenario: A bundled or configured seconv executable hangs on malformed SRT, an interactive prompt, filesystem I/O, or a child process. The worker remains blocked after OCR, cannot observe stop intent, and can prevent job completion and safe application shutdown indefinitely.
evidence: Lines 951-954 invoke Start-Process with -Wait and no timeout parameter or asynchronous poll loop.
The branch contains output validation and file cleanup only after Start-Process returns.
A bounded search of Invoke-VobSubSubtitleChecks.ps1 and Invoke-SubtitleLongWorkHeartbeatChecks.ps1 found no seconv, fix-common-errors, or Start-Process coverage.
Other VobSub extraction/OCR paths use timeout-aware command helpers, showing the lifecycle expectation is available.
existing_safeguards: seconv cleanup is optional and runs only when an executable is found.
Output is accepted only if it remains usable and retains a cue-count floor.
Temporary stdout/stderr/backup files are removed after the process returns.
safeguard_gap: Post-return validation cannot help when the external process never returns, and optionality makes the bug machine/configuration dependent rather than bounded.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-VobSubSubtitleChecks.ps1 covers OCR and validation paths.
ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-SubtitleLongWorkHeartbeatChecks.ps1 covers other long subtitle work.
tests_missing: Hung seconv timeout and process-tree kill
Stop-flag interruption during seconv cleanup
Heartbeat continuity and cleanup-file recovery on timeout
recommended_remediation: Run seconv through the canonical timeout/stop-aware native process helper with bounded stdout/stderr capture, heartbeat callbacks, and child-tree termination. Treat cleanup timeout as a warning and restore the validated pre-seconv SRT.
remediation_risk: Medium: process-wrapper migration must preserve arguments, redirection, Unicode paths, and the intentional fallback to the pre-seconv copy.
validation_rung: Synthetic fake-seconv tests for success, nonzero exit, hang, spawned child, stop request, and timeout, followed by VobSub and subtitle long-work unit suites. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root; archived W05 process review did not cover the optional seconv post-processing branch.

title: Scratch subtitle conversion checks no-clobber before work but commits with an overwriting replace
observed_behavior: The stage rejects an SRT that exists during initial path validation, then performs parsing, planning, fingerprint checks, and evidence creation before os.replace commits the output. A file created at the target by another operation during that window is overwritten despite the advertised existing-output rejection.
expected_invariant: A scratch stage that promises to create a new sidecar and rejects existing output must enforce no-clobber atomically at commit, not only in an earlier time-of-check.
root_cause: Existence validation and destination commit are separate filesystem operations, and the atomic writer uses replacement semantics rather than an exclusive-create or compare-and-swap protocol.
failure_scenario: Two operation IDs target the same scratch ASS sidecar, or another process creates the sibling SRT after validation. The later stage replaces the first output and both evidence records can describe completion against one shared path, weakening rollback and provenance.
evidence: Lines 93-94 reject output_path only when it already exists at validation time.
Lines 219-240 create operation-specific evidence after that check.
Lines 52-60 commit through os.replace, which overwrites a target that appeared after validation.
Existing stage tests exercise sequential boundaries and operation evidence but do not coordinate competing commits.
existing_safeguards: Input and output must remain inside a source-disjoint scratch root.
Existing output is rejected in the sequential case.
Operation evidence paths are UUID-specific and output hashes are verified after writing.
safeguard_gap: Source isolation limits impact to scratch, but it does not make two successful evidence records for one clobbered destination truthful or preserve an unrelated scratch artifact.
tests_present: tests/python/core/subtitles/test_stage_subtitle_convert.py covers dry-run fingerprints, boundaries, sequential existing-output rejection, evidence, and rollback.
tests_missing: Two coordinated operations racing on the same sibling SRT
Target creation between validation and commit
Exclusive commit and evidence ownership under Windows filesystem semantics
recommended_remediation: Use an exclusive destination reservation or no-replace atomic commit tied to the operation ID. Recheck identity under the reservation, and make rollback delete only an output whose ownership token/hash matches the current operation.
remediation_risk: Medium: Windows atomic no-replace semantics and crash recovery require care. Keep all changes scratch-only and preserve the existing source-root boundary.
validation_rung: Deterministic concurrency tests with barriers around validation and commit on the bundled Python runtime, plus stage mutation and path-boundary suites. Real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root; archived W05 reviews did not cover scratch stage commit races.

category: video stream mapping and decision parity
title: Python plans only the first video stream while FFmpeg encode commands map every non-attached video stream
observed_behavior: The Python decision selects source.video_streams[0] and emits one VideoStreamDecision and one planned video summary. The PowerShell encode builder maps 0:V, which selects all non-attached video streams, and applies the shared video codec flags to that output set. A synthetic two-video source produced one planned action for index 0 while the command topology remains map-all.
expected_invariant: Every video stream selected by an encode/remux command must have an explicit backend-authored action, output codec/policy, and verification expectation, or the command must map only the single planned stream.
root_cause: The decision contract models video as one scalar primary action while the command builder independently uses an all-video FFmpeg selector.
failure_scenario: A source contains a main feature plus a second non-attached video stream with a different codec, resolution, or purpose. Preview and evidence describe only the first stream, but FFmpeg copies or encodes both under shared flags, producing unplanned output tracks or failing on the secondary stream.
evidence: routing.py line 53 chooses only the first video stream and lines 98-103 place one scalar video action in StreamActionSet.
routing_outputs.py lines 112-117 and 159-172 summarize and configure only the primary stream.
encode_policy_arguments.ps1 lines 315-318 deliberately map 0:V, all non-attached video streams.
A bundled-Python synthetic source with video indexes 0 and 99 returned one planned video action for index 0.
existing_safeguards: 0:V excludes attached cover-art streams.
Most common media fixtures contain one video stream.
Output media verification can detect some post-encode track mismatches.
safeguard_gap: Excluding attachments does not constrain genuine secondary video streams, and post-write verification cannot make the pre-execution decision evidence complete.
tests_present: tests/python/core/decide/test_processing_decision.py covers single-video fixtures.
ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-EncodeFlagPolicyChecks.ps1 intentionally asserts 0:V command topology.
tests_missing: Two non-attached video streams with different codecs/resolutions
Exact plan-to-command stream-index parity
Explicit policy for secondary video preservation, drop, or per-stream encode
recommended_remediation: Choose and document one policy: either model video actions as a per-stream list and generate per-stream codec/filter arguments, or map only the explicitly planned primary video stream and record dropped secondary streams. Extend output verification to the selected policy.
remediation_risk: High: changing map-all behavior can remove legitimate alternate video tracks, while per-stream encoding changes FFmpeg argument topology and size policy. Validate representative multi-video fixtures before release.
validation_rung: Synthetic multi-video SourceMediaInfo decision tests, exact FFmpeg argument tests, output-track verification fixtures, and representative multi-video real-media validation before changing production mapping.
prior_audit_relationship: Current exact-byte revalidation of the archived 2026-06-11 W05 multi-video plan/command mismatch; no archived status was inherited.

title: Any sparse ActiveOverrides map silently disables the global RemoveKaraoke policy
observed_behavior: Convert-AssToSrt chooses ActiveOverrides.RemoveKaraoke whenever the overall override map is nonempty, even when that key is absent. PowerShell resolves the missing property to null, the truth test emits helper argument 0, and ass_to_srt keeps karaoke syllable events instead of honoring a global RemoveKaraoke=true setting.
expected_invariant: A sparse per-library/show/folder/file override map must replace only keys it explicitly contains; an unrelated routing, video, audio, or subtitle override must not reset global ASS filtering policy.
root_cause: The resolver tests whether ActiveOverrides itself is truthy rather than whether the dictionary contains the RemoveKaraoke key, unlike neighboring effective-setting helpers that use ContainsKey before overriding a global value.
failure_scenario: A job receives only RoutingProfile, OutputContainer, audio, or another sparse override while global RemoveKaraoke is enabled. The ASS helper receives 0, keeps karaoke animation/syllable events, and publishes an SRT compatibility track whose content silently violates the configured global policy.
evidence: ass.ps1 lines 90-92 read ActiveOverrides.RemoveKaraoke for every nonempty map, without ContainsKey or a null fallback.
Merge-MediaPipelineActiveOverrides returns any nonempty sparse dictionary, and pipeline_processing.ps1 installs that dictionary as script:ActiveOverrides before subtitle conversion.
ass_to_srt_cli.py lines 579-583 interpret positional 0 as remove_karaoke=false; ass_events.py applies the karaoke filter only when that value is true.
An isolated no-write probe with global RemoveKaraoke=true emitted helper argument 1 with no overrides and argument 0 with ActiveOverrides={RoutingProfile='manual'}.
The current ASS regression and heartbeat tests use ActiveOverrides=null, while the library-profile test proves sparse maps are normal but never connects one to Convert-AssToSrt.
affected_flows: library, show, folder, and file override precedence
subtitle compatibility sidecars and embedded converted tracks
existing_safeguards: The global RemoveKaraoke default is true and the Python helper defaults to removing karaoke when its positional value is omitted.
Adjacent ASS style include/exclude overrides fall back to globals when their keys are absent or empty.
Original ASS preservation policy can retain the source-format track independently of the converted SRT.
safeguard_gap: PowerShell always supplies an explicit positional karaoke argument, so the Python default cannot repair the missing-key resolution. Preserving the original ASS track does not make the converted SRT comply with the selected policy.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Legacy/Invoke-LegacyDesktopReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1 checks RemoveKaraoke with ActiveOverrides unset.
ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-SubtitleLongWorkHeartbeatChecks.ps1 exercises ASS conversion with ActiveOverrides unset.
ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-LibraryProfileRoutingChecks.ps1 proves sparse ActiveOverrides maps occur in normal policy composition.
tests_missing: Global RemoveKaraoke=true with a nonempty override map that omits RemoveKaraoke
Explicit per-job RemoveKaraoke=false and true precedence cases
Table-driven parity for every sparse ASS-only override key
recommended_remediation: Resolve RemoveKaraoke through Get-EffectiveSubtitleSwitch or use IDictionary.ContainsKey('RemoveKaraoke') before reading the override; otherwise fall back to script:RemoveKaraoke. Add sparse-map and explicit true/false precedence tests around the exact helper argument.
remediation_risk: Low: the change restores key-by-key override semantics for one boolean. Preserve explicit false values and validate all global, absent-key, true, and false combinations.
validation_rung: Focused ASS conversion, library-profile override, subtitle builder, and reliability tests plus representative ASS real-media validation before changing production behavior. The audit reproduction itself required no real media.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-audit root; prior W05 evidence checked the ordinary global flag path but did not combine ASS conversion with a sparse unrelated ActiveOverrides map.

title: Family-priority early returns discard every lower-priority subtitle failure family
observed_behavior: The subtitle builders can accumulate failures from ASS, TX3G, BDPGS, and VobSub conversion loops into one array. Register-SubtitleExtractionFailure filters that array by family, registers only the first nonempty family in fixed BDPGS, VobSub, ASS, TX3G priority, passes only that subset into subtitle_failure_details, and returns before recording the remaining families.
expected_invariant: When one encode/remux attempt reports multiple subtitle failures, durable source-failure evidence must preserve every supplied code, reason, stream, repro path, and family, even if one primary family determines the top-level classification and suggested action.
root_cause: Sequential family-specific branches each build evidence from a filtered subset and immediately return; there is no aggregate payload or linked child-record step before the primary family is selected.
failure_scenario: A media file has failing BDPGS OCR plus an ASS conversion, VobSub OCR, or TX3G extraction failure in the same builder pass. The durable marker exposes only BDPGS details. The operator repairs that prerequisite and retries only to discover a previously known second failure, while command history and recovery evidence never show that the backend already observed it.
evidence: builders.ps1 uses one shared failures list and independently appends failures from ASS, TX3G, BDPGS, VobSub, and review-routing branches before returning it to encode/remux callers.
encode_preflight.ps1 and remux_subtitle_plan.ps1 pass the complete builder Failures array to Register-SubtitleExtractionFailure once.
failure_records.ps1 lines 133-187 filter each family, call ConvertTo-SubtitleFailureEvidence on only that family, and return after the first match.
An isolated no-write four-family probe produced one registered source failure with family=bdpgs, failure_count=1, and no ASS, VobSub, or TX3G detail despite input_count=4.
Existing reliability checks exercise malformed, ASS-only, BDPGS-only, and unknown-only lists; no test passes mixed families.
affected_flows: ASS, TX3G, BDPGS, and VobSub conversion failures
existing_safeguards: Every individual conversion branch creates a structured failure record before returning to the builder.
The selected family preserves up to twelve same-family details and reports a truncated count.
The top-level source failure is fail-closed and prevents media output from proceeding after any subtitle conversion failure.
safeguard_gap: Fail-closed execution prevents a bad publish but does not preserve the unselected failure records. The lower-level structured evidence exists in memory and is deliberately omitted when the first family branch returns.
tests_present: ops/pipeline/tests/Legacy/Invoke-LegacyDesktopReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1 covers individual ASS, BDPGS, malformed, and empty failure inputs.
ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-RemuxSplitStageChecks.ps1 covers the remux caller's terminal failure handoff.
tests_missing: Two and four mixed subtitle failure families
Preservation of every stream, reason, code, and repro path in aggregate evidence
Deterministic primary-family selection without loss of secondary-family details
Retry classification when mixed persistent and transient subtitle failures coexist
recommended_remediation: Build one aggregate evidence object from the full failure list, with per-family groups and total/truncated counts, before selecting a primary family for the top-level code, classification, and action. Alternatively persist linked child records for every family. Add order-independent mixed-family tests.
remediation_risk: Medium: family-specific retry classifications and operator actions differ, so the primary-code rule must remain explicit and secondary records must not accidentally schedule duplicate work.
validation_rung: Focused failure-record, subtitle builder, encode/remux handoff, failure-registry, and recovery-evidence tests, followed by representative mixed-subtitle real-media validation before changing production behavior. The audit reproduction itself required no real media.
prior_audit_relationship: Distinct from CPA-2026-07-19-007: that finding concerns retry classification for persistent prerequisites; this finding concerns loss of already-collected mixed-family evidence before registration.
